title: How Rockville Basements and I-270 Pollen Load Your Air Ducts
headline: Montgomery County humidity, cool basement trunks, and why registers get dusty again
description: Rockville, MD colonials and townhomes sit on humid basement air and a heavy pollen season. Learn why ducts sweat, how I-270 corridor dust adds to the load, and when to clean.

sections.heading: Rockville’s housing was built for families — and full basements
paragraphs: Twinbrook ranches, Hungerford colonials, King Farm townhomes, and Town Center condos do not look alike. Most of them still share two facts: a basement or a cool mechanical closet, and Montgomery County summer humidity. The I-270 corridor also moves a lot of traffic dust. Returns do not sort pollen from brake dust. They pull both.

When the air conditioner runs, basement supply trunks get cold. Maryland air stays wet. That is condensation on metal, then a sticky film, then the odor you notice when the system starts after a storm.

sections.heading: The basement air handler is doing two jobs
paragraphs: It cools the house. It also sits in the dampest room. If the ducts were never sealed well — common on 1960s–80s systems — humid air leaks in at the joints. Dust from the last pollen season is already inside. Together they are what mold needs.
Townhomes near Twinbrook Metro add a second problem: dryer vents that turn three times before the cap. Lint packs. Moisture blows back into the laundry.
If wiping the registers only lasts a few days, start with [air duct cleaning in Rockville, MD](/locations/rockville).

sections.heading: Typical signs in a Rockville house
paragraphs: You do not need a lab test to decide the system is overdue. Watch for:
listItems: Musty air from basement supplies in July and August.
Gray film on upstairs registers during peak pollen.
A dryer that needs two cycles and a hot laundry closet.

listItems: Dehumidify the basement in summer and keep indoor humidity under 50%.
Change filters when pollen is heavy, not only at the printed interval.
Clean ducts every 3 to 5 years; clear dryer vents about once a year.

faq.q: Why do Rockville basements make air ducts smell musty?
faq.a: Cool metal trunks in a humid basement sweat. Dust and pollen stick to that moisture. The blower then pushes the odor upstairs when the AC or heat starts.

faq.q: Is the I-270 corridor dust a real indoor-air issue?
faq.a: Traffic dust is one more particle load on top of tree pollen. Returns pull it in. Cleaning the ducts removes what filters never caught.
